  MINUTES
  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, JUNE 16, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Ybarra called the meeting to order at 9:04 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  Mayor Ybarra led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Melissa Ybarra, Mayor
  Jesus Rivera, Mayor Pro Tem
  Crystal Larios, Council Member
  Judith Merlo, Council Member
  Monica Rodriguez, Council Member

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
  Zaynah Moussa-Milward, City Attorney
  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk
  Alice Hui, Finance Director/City Treasurer
  Veronica Petrosyan, Health and Environmental Control Director
  Su Tan, Human Resources Director
  Robert Sousa, Police Chief
  Dan Wall, Public Works Director-City Engineer
  Todd Dusenberry, Public Utilities General Manager
  Angela Kimmey, Public Utilities Deputy General Manager
  Richard Corbi, Public Utilities Assistant General Manager
  Joanna Hurtado-Moreno, Water Administrator

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried
  unanimously.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 2 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  PUBLIC COMMENT
  City Clerk Rocha announced that a written comment was received from Edward
  Hernandez concerning data centers, and that a copy had been provided to each
  member and that the comment was available online for public review.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Employee Service Pin Awards
  Recommendation: Recognize May 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report, and the City Council
  recognized the May 2026 Employee Service Pin Award recipients: Building and
  Planning Supervisor, Wesley Cruz; Police Sergeant, Anthony Encinas; Water
  Maintenance Worker, Daniel Gomez; Police Records Technician, Ailin Huynh; and
  Procurement Specialist, Efren Peregrina.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Ybarra, asked if
  any member wished to pull any item. Council Member Larios indicated that she
  would like to discuss Item No. 11. Mayor Ybarra called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar with the exception of Item No. 11. The question
  was called and the motion carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  2.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the June 2, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  3.  Claims Against the City
  Recommendation: Receive and file the claim submitted by Adam Willis.
  4.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 175, for the
  period of May 3, 2026 through May 16, 2026, totaling $7,453,726.95 and consisting
  of ratification of electronic payments totaling $7,276,593.36 and ratification of the
  issuance of early checks totaling $177,133.59.
  5.  Franchise Towing Services Agreement
  Recommendation: Adopt Ordinance No. 1313 granting a Franchise Towing
  Services Agreement to Mr. C’s Towing of South Gate, Inc.
  6.  Fire Department Activity Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the April 2026 Fire Department Activity Report.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  7.  Police Department Activity Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the April 2026 Police Department Activity
  Report.
  8.  Property and Casualty Insurance Placements for Fiscal Year 2026-27
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute all
  related documents to procure the City’s annual insurance coverage for Fiscal Year
  2026-27, effective July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, for a total amount not-to-
  exceed $5,587,684.
  9.  City Housing Report
  Recommendation: Receive and file the City Housing Report presented at the
  Special Vernon Housing Commission Meeting on April 28, 2026.
  10.  Application for 2026 Tree City USA Designation
  Recommendation: Authorize the Mayor to sign and the Public Works Department
  to submit a 2026 Tree City USA Application to the Arbor Day Foundation.
  12.  Blanket Purchase Order with The Home Depot
  Recommendation: Approve the issuance of a blanket Purchase Order with The
  Home Depot in an amount not-to-exceed $234,250 to procure supplies for the
  Public Works Department and Vernon Public Utilities for operational needs and
  special projects for Fiscal Year 2026-27.
  13.  Master Sales Agreement with Itron, Inc.
  Recommendation: A. Find that the best interests of the City are served by a direct
  award of an agreement with Itron, Inc. (Itron) without a competitive selection
  process, pursuant to Vernon Municipal Code Section (VMC) 3.32.110(B)(2); B.
  Pursuant to Sections 3.32.220(B) and 3.32.110(B)(3) of the VMC, find that it is
  commercially unreasonable to rebid the proposed agreement for support and
  maintenance every three years, as Software as a Service (Saas), software license,
  firmware, and equipment, and maintenance services for existing City utility meters
  are only available through Itron; and C. Approve and authorize the City
  Administrator to execute a Master Sales Agreement with Itron, in substantially the
  same form as submitted, for utility metering hardware, software, and maintenance
  services in an amount not-to-exceed $285,229.68 for a five-year term.
  14.  Support and Maintenance Agreement with Advanced Utility Systems
  Recommendation: A. Pursuant to Sections 3.32.220(B) and 3.32.110(B)(3) of the
  Vernon Municipal Code (VMC), find that it is commercially unreasonable to rebid
  the proposed agreement for support and maintenance every three years, as a
  substantial upgrade to the billing system has recently been completed, the
  software platform is proprietary to Advanced Utility Systems, a division of N. Harris
  Computer Corporation (Advanced), and continuity of support is critical for
  maintaining the reliable operation of the City’s utility billing system; and B. Approve
  and authorize the City Administrator to execute a Support and Maintenance
  Agreement with Advanced, in substantially the same form as submitted, to provide
  software support and maintenance to the Infinity Customer Information System
  (CIS) billing system in an amount not-to-exceed $446,604.60 for a five-year term.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 4 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  The following item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for individual
  consideration:

  11.  Amendment No.1 to Services Agreement with Interwest Consulting Group,
  Inc., Contract No. 20250081
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute
  Amendment No.1 to the Services Agreement with Interwest Consulting Group,
  Inc., in substantially the same form as submitted, for On-Call Building Plan Checks
  and Inspection Services, for a total amount not to exceed $2,500,000 in additional
  funds.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Council Member Larios inquired whether there would be an extension of cost and
  time, or just of cost, and requested clarification on the reason. Public Works
  Director Wall explained that there would only be an increase in costs. Interwest
  Consulting Group collects a portion of the fees charged, and the increase is due
  to the volume of development activity in the City over the last two years, which has
  required extensive coordination between applicants and Interwest Consulting
  Group. Because the projects were high-value, the funds were exhausted.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Mayor Pro Tem Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve the recommendations for Item No. 11. The question was called and the
  motion carried unanimously.

  NEW BUSINESS

  15.  Public Safety Special Parcel Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026-27
  Recommendation: A. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-027 determining the Public
  Safety Special Parcel Tax levied for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27, pursuant to Vernon
  Municipal Code Section 3.20.020; and B. Approve and authorize the Director of
  Finance to execute an Agreement for Billing Direct Assessments (Public Safety
  Special Parcel Tax) with the County of Los Angeles Auditor-Controller’s Office, in
  substantially the same form as submitted, for the collection and distribution of the
  Public Safety Special Parcel Tax for FY 2026-27.
  Finance Director Hui presented the staff report.
  Mayor Ybarra invited public comment, there being none, and no discussion from
  the City Council, Mayor Ybarra invited a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A, and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 5 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  16.  Warehouse Special Parcel Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026-27
  Recommendation: A. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-028 determining the Warehouse
  Special Parcel Tax levied for Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-27 pursuant to Vernon
  Municipal Code Section 3.20.010; and B. Approve and authorize the Director of
  Finance to execute an Agreement for Billing of Direct Assessments (Warehouse
  Special Parcel Tax) with the County of Los Angeles Auditor-Controller’s Office, in
  substantially the same form as submitted, for the collection and distribution of the
  Warehouse Special Parcel Tax for FY 2026-27.
  Finance Director Hui presented the staff report.
  Mayor Ybarra invited public comment, there being none, and no discussion from
  the City Council, Mayor Ybarra invited a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Merlo moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  17.  Electric Rate Schedules, Energy Cost Adjustment Billing Factor, and
  Renewable Energy Cost Adjustment Factor
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-029 to Amend Electric Rate
  Schedule Nos. CS, D, GS-1, GS-2, LS-1, LS-2, OL-1, PA-1, PA-2, PA-TOU, TC-1,
  TOU-I, TOU GS-1, TOU GS-2, TOU PA-1, TOU-D, TOU-G, TOU-V, TOU-Vt, and
  GP regarding electrical rates to be charged for electrical energy distributed and
  supplied by the City within its boundaries.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra inquired how City staff notified customers of the increase in RPS
  rates, and Public Utilities Assistant General Manager Corbi stated that the City has
  maintained a stable rate and most recently informed customers during the
  information meetings held.

  Mayor Ybarra inquired whether staff were seeing an increase or decrease in prices
  since tariffs were being removed and how staff were recovering costs. Public
  Utilities Assistant General Manager Corbi responded that staff had rejected any
  billings with tariff-associated costs, since the Supreme Court ruled the tariffs were
  unconstitutional, and that they were looking into recovering those costs.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comment, there being none, Mayor Ybarra invited a
  motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to adopt Resolution No. 2026-029 to Amend Electric Rate Schedule Nos. CS, D,
  GS-1, GS-2, LS-1, LS-2, OL-1, PA-1, PA-2, PA-TOU, TC-1, TOU-I, TOU GS-1,
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 6 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  TOU GS-2, TOU PA-1, TOU-D, TOU-G, TOU-V, TOU-Vt, and GP regarding
  electrical rates to be charged for electrical energy distributed and supplied by the
  City within its boundaries. The question was called and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  18.  Amendments to Natural Gas Rule No. 14
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-030 Amending Natural Gas Rule
  No. 14 (Service Connections and Facilities on Customer’s Premises) regarding the
  Rules for Gas Service for gas distributed and supplied by the City within its
  boundaries.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry introduced the Public Utilities Deputy
  General Manager Kimmey, who presented the staff report.

  The Mayor invited public comment, there being none, and no discussion from the
  City Council, Mayor Ybarra invited a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  adopt Resolution No. 2026-030 Amending Natural Gas Rule No. 14 (Service
  Connections and Facilities on Customer’s Premises) regarding the Rules for Gas
  Service for gas distributed and supplied by the City within its boundaries.

  19.  Commission and Committee Appointments
  Recommendation: A. Appoint two (2) Business Representatives, one (1)
  Employee/Labor Representative, and (1) Real Estate Representative to full four-
  year terms (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030) to the Business and Industry
  Commission; B. Appoint one (1) Business Representative, and one (1) Vernon
  Area Representative to full four-year terms (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030) and
  one (1) City Council Representative and one (1) Vernon Area Representative to a
  partial term (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029) to the Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant
  Committee; C. Appoint two (2) Business Representatives to full four-year terms
  (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030) to the Green Vernon Commission; and D. Appoint
  one (1) Resident (Council Member) to a partial term (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029)
  to the Vernon Housing Commission.

  City Clerk Rocha presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra invited public comment, there being none, discussion ensued
  amongst the City Council regarding the appointments.

  Council Member Larios suggested that applicants be encouraged to submit a
  resume with their applications to provide more information for the City Council to
  consider.

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 7 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  Mayor Ybarra and Council Member Rodriguez abstained from proposing
  appointments to the Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee Vernon Area
  Representative due to relatives having submitted applications for consideration.

  The remainder of the City Council proposed appointing Ronit Edry, Leticia Lopez,
  and Brenda Orellana to the Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee.

  Mayor Ybarra invited a motion at the conclusion of the proposed appointments to
  all Commissions and Committees.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  appoint Catherine Browne and Ronit Edry as the Business Representatives,
  Jacquie Cabrera as the Employee/Labor Representative, and Miles Solomon as
  the Real Estate Representative to full four-year terms (July 1, 2026 to June 30,
  2030) to the Business and Industry Commission; B. Appoint Ronit Edry as the
  Business Representative, and Leticia Lopez as Vernon Area Representative to full
  four-year terms (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030), and Judith Merlo as City Council
  Representative and Brenda Orellana as Vernon Area Representative to a partial
  term (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029) to the Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant
  Committee; C. Appoint Catherine Browne and Ronit Edry Business
  Representatives to full four-year terms (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2030) to the Green
  Vernon Commission; and D. Appoint Monica Rodriguez as the Resident (Council
  Member) to a partial term (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2029) to the Vernon Housing
  Commission. The question was called and the motion carried unanimously. City
  Clerk Rocha reaffirmed Mayor Ybarra and Council Member Rodriguez’s abstention
  from the appointments to the Vernon CommUnity Fund Grant Committee Area
  Representative.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  20.  Fiscal Year 2026-27 Citywide Annual Operating Budget, Capital Improvement
  Plan, and Appropriations Limit (Gann)
  Recommendation: A. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-031 approving and adopting the
  Annual Operating Budget and the Capital Improvement Plan for Fiscal Year 2026-
  27; and B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-032 adopting the Appropriations Limit for
  Fiscal Year 2026-27 pursuant to Government Code Section 7910.

  City Administrator Saeki presented the staff report. He informed the City Council
  that staff was able to identify cost savings by deferring the hiring of the Public
  Works Superintendent for ½ year, defer the Health Department's Cross Connection
  Program, and the purchase of a vehicle for the police department Detective
  Bureau, which results in a surplus for the General Fund of $324,958, including the
  Vernon City Elementary Interventionist position.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 8 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:49 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:49 a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Merlo seconded a motion to
  defer the following costs savings identified by staff: hiring the Public Works
  Superintendent for ½ year, defer the Cross Connection Program, and the purchase
  of a vehicle for the police department Detective Bureau. The question was called
  and the motion carried unanimously.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Rivera moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A, and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  21.  2025 Urban Water Management Plan
  Recommendation: A. Find that the proposed action is exempt under the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with California Water Code
  Section 10652, which exempts the preparation and adoption of Urban Water
  Management Plan (UWMP) and the Water Shortage Contingency Plan (WSCP),
  collectively referred to herein as the 2025 UWMP, from CEQA requirements, and
  CEQA Guideline Section 15061(b)(3), the general rule that CEQA only applies to
  activities that may have a significant effect on the environment, because the plan
  referenced herein is merely an update of the existing 2020 UWMP; and
  B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-033 Adopting the 2025 UWMP.

  Public Utilities General Manager Dusenberry introduced Water Administrator
  Hurtado-Moreno, who presented the staff report.

  Mayor Ybarra opened the public hearing at 9:55 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Ybarra closed the public hearing at 9:56 a.m.

  Mayor Ybarra invited further Council discussion. There being none, Mayor Ybarra
  called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rodriguez seconded a motion
  to approve recommendations A, and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried unanimously.

  ORAL REPORTS
  22.  City Administrator Reports on Activities and Other Announcements
 Docusign Envelope ID: 834B3FA3-A90E-8E5A-825A-EAD1B6BB08F6

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 9 of 9
  June 16, 2026

  City Administrator Saeki announced the Business Breakfast information meeting
  would take place on Wednesday, June 3rd, at 8:30 a.m. in the Council Chambers.

  23.  Council Reports on Activities (including AB 1234), Announcements, or
  Directives to Staff

  None.

  CLOSED SESSION
  At 9:55 a.m., Mayor Ybarra recessed the meeting to Closed Session.
  24.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2)
  Significant exposure to litigation (1 potential matter)

  RECONVENE
  At 10:41 a.m., Mayor Ybarra adjourned the Closed Session and reconvened the
  regular meeting.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
  City Attorney Moussa-Milward reported that the City Council met in Closed
  Session, discussed the item on the agenda, provided direction, and took no
  reportable action.
  ADJOURNMENT
  Mayor Ybarra adjourned the meeting at 10:41 a.m.
